title: Scenario: Clairvoyance at the Final Table

lines.text: Chapter eleven, section four. Scenario, clairvoyance at the final table.
Return one more time to the clairvoyance game, but now imagine the two players are at a tournament final table with three players remaining and a big ICM cliff between second and third place.
Ivan has an ace or a queen, Opal has a king, and Ivan can bet or check as in the original game.
In the cash-game version, we solved this game with a specific bluffing frequency for the queen and a specific calling frequency for the king.
At the final table, the ICM cost of losing the pot is much larger than the ICM gain of winning it, especially for the shorter stack.

The correct adjustment is that Opal's calling frequency should shrink, because the ICM cost of a wrong call is amplified, and Ivan's bluffing frequency with the queen should shrink in response, because he now needs less bluffing to make Opal indifferent.
Notice the direction of the adjustment: less action from both sides, more folding, and less thin value pursuit.
That is the general final-table ICM lesson: the game gets more conservative for both players when the payoff of a loss is much worse than the payoff of a win.
The polarized attacker keeps most of the leverage, but he has to spend it more carefully, and the bluff-catcher has to accept a lower expected value from her showdown holdings.
When you feel a hand tightening up on you at the final table, that instinct is often ICM speaking, and following it is usually the right call.
